**ReLU function:** $\text{ReLU}(z) = \max(0, z)$.

## Problem 1. LASSO (30 points)

This is a **regression problem**: we want to predict a numeric target $y$ from two inputs, $x_1$ and $x_2$, using the data below.

| $x_1$ | $x_2$ | $y$ |
|:-----:|:-----:|:-----:|
| 1 | 0 | -2 |
| 2 | 1 | 0 |
| 3 | -2 | -1 |
| 4 | 3 | 1 |

Consider these four models:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Model A:} \quad \hat{y} &= -2 + 0.5 x_1 + 0.25 x_2 \\
\text{Model B:} \quad \hat{y} &= -1.25 + 0.25 x_1 + 0.25 x_2 \\
\text{Model C:} \quad \hat{y} &= -0.5 + 0 x_1 + 0.25 x_2 \\
\text{Model D:} \quad \hat{y} &= -0.5 + 0 x_1 + 0 x_2
\end{aligned}
$$

Each model has the form $\hat{y} = w_0 + w_1 x_1 + w_2 x_2$. Its total squared loss is $L(w_0, w_1, w_2) = \sum (\hat{y} - y)^2$. LASSO adds a penalty on the size of the slopes $w_1$ and $w_2$. The best model is the one with the smallest **objective**:

$$\text{Objective} = L(w_0, w_1, w_2) + \alpha \left( |w_1| + |w_2| \right)$$

The number $\alpha$ sets how strong the penalty is. The intercept $w_0$ is not penalized.

a. (6 points) Which of the four models is best when $\alpha = 0$? With $\alpha = 0$ there is no penalty, so this is the ordinary linear model.

b. (6 points) Which of the four models is best when $\alpha = 4$?

c. (6 points) Which of the four models is best when $\alpha = 7$?

d. (6 points) Which of the four models is best when $\alpha = 10$?

e. (6 points) As $\alpha$ increases, what happens to the slopes of the best model?

## Problem 2. Image Recognition (CNN) (40 points)

A CNN takes the $5 \times 5$ grayscale image $X$ and applies the $2 \times 2$ filter $K$ (bias 0, stride 1, no padding).

$$
X = \begin{bmatrix}
1 & 0 & 3 & 3 & 0 \\
0 & 1 & 3 & 2 & 0 \\
0 & 0 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\
1 & 0 & 3 & 3 & 0 \\
0 & 0 & 1 & 2 & 0
\end{bmatrix}
\qquad
K = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}
$$

The convolution gives the $4 \times 4$ feature map below. Its first row is missing.

$$
\text{Feature map} = \begin{bmatrix}
\boxed{\ ?_1\ } & \boxed{\ ?_2\ } & \boxed{\ ?_3\ } & \boxed{\ ?_4\ } \\
1 & 4 & 0 & -4 \\
-1 & 5 & 1 & -5 \\
-1 & 4 & 1 & -5
\end{bmatrix}
$$

**Present your solution the way the sample solution does:** draw the grids of squares and the network, and write each calculation next to the drawing.

a. (12 points) Compute the first row of the feature map, $?_1$, $?_2$, $?_3$ and $?_4$. For each one, draw the image as a grid of squares and box the $2 \times 2$ window, then write out filter $\times$ window (multiply the matching numbers and add).

b. (10 points) Apply ReLU to the feature map, then $2 \times 2$ max pooling to get a $2 \times 2$ map. Draw the feature map, the map after ReLU, and the pooled map as grids of squares. Outline the four $2 \times 2$ pooling blocks and write the max of each block.

c. (4 points) Flatten the pooled map row by row into $\mathbf{a} = (a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4)$. Draw $\mathbf{a}$ as a row of 4 squares.

d. (8 points) Dense layer: $z_A = 0.2a_1 + 0.2a_3$ and $z_B = a_2 + a_4$ (biases 0). Draw the network: 4 input nodes $a_1, \dots, a_4$, 2 output nodes $z_A, z_B$, and a line from each input to each output labeled with its weight (dashed for weight 0). Compute both scores.

e. (6 points) Softmax: compute $p_A$ and $p_B$. Use $e^1 \approx 2.72$ and $e^2 \approx 7.39$. Add the softmax step to your network drawing: an arrow from each score to its probability node. Which class is predicted?

## Problem 3. Recommendation System (30 points)

A podcast app gives every podcast a 2-number embedding (number 1: news and business, number 2: comedy and stories). **These podcast embeddings were learned beforehand** by the app's model from all users' listening data, so in this problem they are **known**. Only Sarah's embedding must be computed.

| Podcast | Embedding (news, comedy) |
|:---:|:---:|
| Podcast A | (0.8, 0.2) |
| Podcast B | (0.2, 0.9) |
| Podcast C | (0.6, 0.6) |
| Podcast D | (0.1, 0.4) |
| Podcast E | (0.9, 0.8) |
| Podcast F | (0.1, 1.2) |

Last month **Sarah** listened to **Podcast E** and **Podcast F**.

a. (6 points) Compute **Sarah's embedding** as the **average** of the podcasts she listened to.

b. (6 points) Score every podcast with the **dot product**. Recommend the top 2 that Sarah has **not** heard.

**One week later.** Sarah played **Podcast C** and **Podcast D**; she skipped Podcast B. Three **new** podcasts were also released this week (their embeddings were also learned beforehand):

| New this week | Embedding (news, comedy) |
|:---:|:---:|
| Podcast G | (1.0, 0.5) |
| Podcast H | (0.1, 1.0) |
| Podcast I | (0.7, 0.9) |

c. (9 points) Recompute Sarah's embedding as a **weighted average** of her 4 plays: older plays (E, F) count **1**, this week's plays (C, D) count **2**. Score the 5 podcasts she has not heard (A, B, G, H, I) and recommend the top 2.

d. (9 points) Sarah also gave **feedback**: she **liked** Podcast D and tapped **"not interested"** on Podcast C. The app doubles the weight of a liked play and gives a "not interested" play weight **$-1$**. Recompute her embedding and her top 2.
